title: No lo perdiste
desc: A phone gone, and a grammar that puts the blame nowhere
setting: You got off the bus with an empty pocket and you are telling Marcos about it badly.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.en: What happened, man? Look at your face.

options.es: Me robaron el celular en el bus.
options.en: They stole my phone on the bus.
options.feedback: Me robaron, with no subject at all. Spanish tells this whole story without ever naming who did it.
You did not lose it. Marcos is about to correct you, and the correction is worth more than the phone.
Understood, and constructed like English. Nobody here says it that way.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: No lo perdiste, maje. Te lo robaron. No es lo mismo.
steps.en: You did not lose it, maje. It was stolen from you. Not the same thing.

options.es: Cierto. Se me olvida esa diferencia.
options.en: True. I keep forgetting that difference.
options.feedback: And listen to what you just said: se me olvida. The language keeps doing it to you, which is exactly the point he is making.
Fine. He was opening a door onto a whole piece of grammar and you closed it politely.

options.es: Es igual, ya no lo tengo.
options.en: It is the same, I do not have it any more.
options.feedback: Not to him. Here the bad things happen to you, and the words are arranged to say so.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.es: Aquí las cosas malas le pasan a uno. Se me cayó, se me perdió, se me olvidó.
steps.en: Here the bad things happen to you. It fell on me, it got lost on me, it slipped my mind.

options.es: Entonces se me quedó la bolsa en la casa.
options.en: So my bag got left at the house on me.
options.feedback: You built one yourself out of a different verb. That is the moment a pattern stops being a rule and starts being yours.

options.en: I see how it works now.
options.feedback: Probably. Saying one of your own out loud is what makes it true.
It is not an excuse, it is how the language is built. A dropped glass has no culprit in Spanish.

steps.speaker: Marcos
steps.en: And what are you going to do now?

options.es: Nada. Se me fue y ya. ¿O vos qué harías?
options.en: Nothing. It is gone and that is that. Or what would you do?
options.feedback: Se me fue, again with no culprit, and then you asked the man who lives here. He will tell you what people actually do, which is mostly nothing.

options.en: I am going to buy another one tomorrow.
options.feedback: Practical. He was asking a slightly bigger question than that.

options.es: Voy a buscar al que me lo robó.
options.en: I am going to go looking for whoever stole it.
options.feedback: In a bus with forty people in it there is nobody to look for. Marcos will spend ten minutes talking you out of this.
